scientificStatus: Numerical geometric verification only. This does not prove exact rotational symmetry, anticoherence, or optimality.

api.points: Array of {x,y,z,multiplicity} objects or [x,y,z,weight] arrays; weight defaults to1.
api.rotationCount: Finite count includes the identity; null for a continuous group.
api.axes: Unoriented directions. order is the cyclic order; null denotes all rotation angles about that axis. angle/generatorAngle are2pi/order for finite axes.
api.continuousFamilies: Equal antipodal weights have an additional continuous family of perpendicular half-turn axes; these are not replaced by arbitrary sampled axes.
api.cache: Cached by array identity plus complete coordinate/weight signature; clearCache() is available.

method.enumeration: Choose a pair with maximal cross-product norm. An exact proper rotation is uniquely determined by its images. Enumerate all ordered image pairs with the same multiplicities and Gram product, and form the oriented-frame rotation.
method.verification: A complete bipartite matching checks every point with its original multiplicity at the chord-distance tolerance.
method.axisExtraction: Quaternion branches, including largest-diagonal branches at pi, give stable axes. Unoriented axes are coalesced and assigned the largest detected cyclic order.
method.continuousCases: A single point or collinear antipodal set has arbitrary rotations about its line. Equal antipodal weights also permit every perpendicular half-turn axis.
method.limitations: A tolerance-based detection is not a symbolic proof. Near-collinear and near-coincident configurations are explicitly flagged; absence of a detected axis is not a certified nonexistence result.

continuousFamilies.description: Every axis perpendicular to the main axis gives a half-turn symmetry.
